section: common mistakes
text: Common mistakes "Reward and value are the same." Reward is one step's signal; value is the expected sum of what follows. "The observation is the state." One frame, or the last chat message, can leave out what the future depends on. "γ = 1 is always wrong." It is standard when every episode ends, as in language-model RL. "Model-based means a learned model." Dynamic programming and AlphaZero use a given one. "The reward model makes RLHF model-based." Nothing plans with it; it stands in for the reward. "On-policy means online, off-policy means offline." Q-learning is off-policy while interacting; PPO reuses each batch for several epochs and is still approximately on-policy. "Any learned baseline makes an actor-critic." REINFORCE with a baseline, RLOO and GRPO never bootstrap from it, so they are policy-based ( Sutton and Barto §13.5 ). "Deep RL is a different theory." Its targets are the classical ones; what is new is function approximation and the tricks that keep it stable. "Token generation is a hard environment." The transition is trivial; credit assignment and a trustworthy reward are the hard parts. "A higher reward means a better model." With a proxy reward, the policy can climb it while true quality falls (reward hacking).
